newsitem.title: FRANCE: Building of new French cargo airport to start Feb.
newsitem.headline: Building of new French cargo airport to start Feb.

text.p: French Transport minister, Bernard Pons, on February 14 will formally start the building work to convert an ex-NATO airfield into an all-cargo airport, the project's management company, SAEM Europort told Reuters.

The airport is at Vatry, 140 kms east of Paris in the Marne department, and one billion francs will be spent by the local authority, (conseil general de la marne) on the project over the next two years, Jean-Claude Reboulin, SEAM's managing director said.
Vatry is close to the A4 and A26 motorways and is also serviced by a railhead.
"The opening of the airport is fixed for mid-1998 with the first all-cargo flights scheduled to operate from this date or at the latest by the end-1998," Reboulin explained.
Initial development work, scheduled to begin at the end of this month, will centre on improving road access to the site with a new roundabout.

"This will be followed by the demolition of existing airfield installations and the construction of a control tower, administrative and service facilities, a freight centre and the lengthening of the runway to 3,860 metres in order to accommodate the full-range of wide-bodied aircraft," Reboulin added.
Europort is targeting the major air cargo markets including North America, the Far East, the Gulf States and Europe.

According to market surveys commissioned by the company, the all-cargo airport could generate between 300,000 and 700,000 tonnes of air cargo annually by 2010 by taking freight business away from Europe's seven leading airports over the next 15 years. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +5017
